root_cause: The same-thread fast path for Atomics.waitAsync()/Atomics.notify() was added without accounting for the fact that JSContext::realm() can differ from the realm of the promise being resolved; the code assumed 'same context' implied 'same realm', which is not guaranteed in a multi-realm embedding like the browser (e.g. cross-origin iframes, Xray wrappers, or other realm-switching operations happening on the same context).
findings: In js::atomics_notify_impl, when Atomics.notify() detects that the async waiter it is about to resolve was created by the *same* JSContext (waiter->cx() == cx), it takes a fast path: instead of dispatching an off-thread task to the event loop, it extracts the PromiseObject directly into a `promisesToResolve` vector and later calls PromiseObject::resolve(cx, promisesToResolve[i], resultMsg) on it a
